segments.text: Not long ago, Google was viewed as the
biggest loser of the AI era. You might
remember Chad, or I mean Bard, Google's
first chat GPT competitor released in
February of 2023. During the live stream
announcement, Bard immediately
hallucinated and crashed Google stock by
9%, and all the experts told us Google
was collapsing under its own
bureaucratic weight. And yet somehow
this week they may have just pulled off
the biggest Mongolian reversal in
history with the release of Gemini 3.
Unlike the Bard disaster, the Gemini 3
release pumped Google stock by 6% to an
all-time high, and they became the
overwhelming favorite to have the best
AI model by the end of the year. In
today's video, we'll find out if Gemini
3 gets us closer to the singularity, or
if Bard just got its hands on some of
Brian Johnson's magic mushrooms. It is
November 21st, 2025, and you are
watching The Code Report. Back in my
day, all the gifted kids would get their
wiggles out by holding Beyblade battles
in between Johnny Bravo reruns. But
nowadays, all the cool kids are
designing elaborate benchmarks to test
the capabilities of the latest AI
models. Like imagine you needed to know
which AI model was the best at detecting
silhouettes of Pokémon, or which was the
best at managing a simulated vending
machine business, or which was the
closest to general intelligence and
therefore most likely to use our meatbag
bodies as an energy source. Regardless
of which one you choose, odds are Gemini
3 Pro is at the top of the list, and
it's not even very close. It swept all
the major LM Arena leaderboards, took
the top spot on Weird ML, Humanities
Last Exam, Math Arena, and many others.
Now, I know trust me, bro benchmarks
aren't everything, but it's been a
minute since we've had a new model
released dominate across so many of them
at the same time. And if you don't
really trust benchmarks, Amp just
replaced Claude with Gemini 3 Pro to
power their coding agent after they
realized it did everything Sonic 4.5
did, but better. That's impressive, but
the AI war is still raging, and Gemini 3
wasn't even the most interesting
announcement from Google. They also
unveiled a brand new technology called
anti-gravity, a new electromagnetic
propulsion device that allows cars to
fly just like in Back to the Future II.
I wish that were true, but no,
anti-gravity is actually just another VS
Code fork designed for agentic coding
with Gemini. You might remember back in
July when the co-founders of Windsurf
suddenly ditched their employees and
with a non-exclusive license to the tech
joined Google in a $2.4 billion deal. We
haven't heard much about it since, but
this week we're finally seeing the
aftermath of that with the release of
anti-gravity, a new agentic development
platform led by the former Windsurf
co-founders. According to the
announcement video, Congratulations.
You have been elevated to a manager of
agents. In other words, the AI figured
out how to use you as a meatbag energy
source before it even got to AGI. My
favorite feature is when they forgot to
rename Cascade, which is the name of
Windsurf's coding agent. And yes, if
you're following along at home, it's
turtles all the way down. Their biggest
competitor is obviously Chad, the brain
rot IDE backed by Y Combinator. Unlike
every other editor, Chad integrates your
brain rot vices directly into your
agentic coding workflow, allowing you to
gamble, watch TikTok, or even swipe on
Tinder while your agents do work for you
in the background. Next on the list is
Google's other editor IDX, which unlike
anti-gravity is web-based. Oh, never
mind, it looks like that's dead, and
it's now called Firebase Studio, which
accelerates your entire development life
cycle with AI agents, which is kind of
